events.void-click: Fires after an enabled button is activated, once any form submit or reset it does has run. Not fired while the button is disabled. A native `click` listener works too.

void-button.children: The label: text, or text with an icon. For an icon-only button put an `aria-label` on the button. A link (`<a href>`) or a native `<button>` can go inside to make a link that looks like a button: the inner element is then the one control (the host has no role and no tab stop, and draws the focus ring when the link has focus). `disabled` marks the link `aria-disabled="true"`, takes it out of the tab order and stops it navigating.

events.void-input: Fires on every edit of the text. `detail.value` is the new text.
events.void-change: Fires when the text is committed (the field loses focus after a change). `detail.value` is the text.
events.void-action: Fires when the action button is pressed. `detail.value` is the current text.

events.void-change: Fires when the user toggles the checkbox. `detail.checked` is the new state and `detail.value` its value.
Fires when a checkbox in the group is toggled. `detail.value` lists the values of the checked boxes.

void-checkbox-group.children: Takes `void-checkbox` children. The `label` attribute names the group.

events.void-change: Fires when the colour changes by dragging, typing a hex value or choosing a swatch; `detail.value` is the hex string. It fires continuously while dragging.
Fires when the user chooses an option. `detail.value` is its value.

void-combobox.children: One `void-combobox-content` holding the `void-option`s, one per choice. The component renders the input before it.

events.void-input: Fires on every edit of the text. `detail.value` is the new text.
events.void-submit: Fires when the user presses the send button or the send key. `detail.value` is the message; the field is cleared afterwards. Not fired when the field is empty or disabled.

events.void-change: Fires when the user picks a day, or types a date that is accepted (on blur or Enter), once per change. `detail.value` is the ISO date (empty when the field was cleared) and `detail.date` the same day as a `Date` (`null` when cleared). A typed date that is refused fires nothing; `error` says why.
Fires when the user picks a day. `detail.value` is the ISO date and `detail.date` the same day as a `Date`.

events.void-input: Fires on every keystroke while editing. `detail.value` is the text so far.
events.void-change: Fires when the user commits an edit (Enter or leaving the field). `detail.value` is the new text.
events.void-cancel: Fires when the user abandons an edit with Escape; the previous value stays.

void-field.children: Exactly one control: a `void-input`, `void-select`, `void-textarea` or another form control. The `label`, `helper` and `error` attributes supply the text around it.

events.void-change: Fires when the chosen files change, by dropping, browsing or removing one. `detail.value` (and `detail.files`) is the list of accepted `File`s.
events.void-reject: Fires, without bubbling, when a dropped or browsed file is refused. `detail.rejected` is a list of `{ file, reason }`, `reason` being `type` (not matched by `accept`), `size` (over `max-size`) or `count` (a further file while `multiple` is off). The zone also sets `error` to a message, which makes the drop zone `aria-invalid` and described by it; the next accepted selection clears it.

events.void-input: Fires on every keystroke. `detail.value` is the new text.
events.void-change: Fires when the value is committed (the field loses focus after a change). `detail.value` is the text.
Fires when an option is selected or deselected. `detail.value` lists every selected value.

void-multiselect.children: One `void-multiselect-content` holding the `void-option`s, one per choice; mark the initial ones with `selected`. The component renders the trigger and its chips before it.

events.void-input: Fires on every keystroke. `detail.value` is the number typed so far, or null while the text is empty or not a number.
events.void-change: Fires when the value is committed: the field loses focus after typing, or the step buttons or arrow keys change it. `detail.value` is the new number and `detail.previous` the old one.

void-option.children: Text, or rich content (an icon, a second line) with `label` giving the plain text shown once it is chosen. Only inside `void-combobox-content` or `void-multiselect-content`.

events.void-input: Fires on every edit of the code. `detail.value` is the characters entered so far.
events.void-change: Fires when focus leaves the cells with a different code from when it came in. `detail.value` is the code.
events.void-complete: Fires once every cell is filled. `detail.value` is the full code.

events.void-change: Fires when the user chooses this radio. `detail.value` is its value and `detail.checked` is true.
Fires when the user chooses a radio. `detail.value` is its value.

void-radio-group.children: Takes `void-radio` children. The `label` attribute names the group.

events.void-change: Fires when the user chooses a segment. `detail.value` is its value.

void-segmented-control-item.children: The label text of one segment.

events.void-change: Fires when the user chooses an option. `detail.value` is its value.

void-select.children: One native `<select>` carrying `name`, `required`, `disabled` and the native `option` and `optgroup` elements; not `void-option`. A prompt is a first `<option value="" disabled selected hidden>`.

events.void-input: Fires continuously while the thumb moves. `detail.value` is the current number.
events.void-change: Fires when the user releases the thumb or uses the keyboard. `detail.value` is the number.
Fires when the user flips the switch. `detail.checked` is the new state and `detail.value` its value.
Fires when a tag is added or removed. `detail.value` is the full list of tags.

events.void-input: Fires on every keystroke. `detail.value` is the new text.
events.void-change: Fires when the value is committed (the field loses focus after a change). `detail.value` is the text.
Fires when the user presses the toggle. `detail.pressed` is the new state and `detail.value` its value.

void-toggle.children: The label text or an icon (give an icon-only toggle an `aria-label`).

events.void-change: Fires when the user presses a toggle. `detail.value` is an array of pressed values with `multiple`, otherwise the pressed value or an empty string.

events.void-open: Fires when the dialog opens. `detail.reason` is `api`: the dialog opens only when you set `open`. It does not bubble.
events.void-close: Fires before the dialog closes, on the dialog only (it does not bubble). `detail.reason` is `escape`, `outside` (the backdrop), `close-button`, `form` (a `method="dialog"` form), `parent` or `api`. Call `preventDefault()` to keep it open when the user caused the close (`escape`, `outside`, `close-button`).

void-dialog.children: Explicit parts, in this order: `void-dialog-title` (names the dialog; required), `void-dialog-description`, `void-dialog-body` and `void-dialog-actions`. A `<form method="dialog">` may wrap them. The parts stay where you write them.

events.void-open: Fires when the drawer opens. `detail.reason` is `api`. It does not bubble.
events.void-close: Fires before the drawer closes, on the drawer only (it does not bubble). `detail.reason` is `escape`, `outside` (the backdrop), `close-button`, `form`, `parent` or `api`. Call `preventDefault()` to keep it open when the user caused the close.

void-drawer.children: The same parts as the dialog: `void-drawer-title`, `void-drawer-description`, `void-drawer-body` and `void-drawer-actions`, in that order.

void-dropdown-menu.children: Two parts: `void-dropdown-menu-trigger`, wrapping the one button that opens the menu, and `void-dropdown-menu-content`, holding the `void-dropdown-menu-item`s (and `void-dropdown-menu-separator`s between groups). Choosing an item closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger; give an item `keep-open` to leave it open.

events.void-open: Fires when the menu opens. `detail.reason` is `trigger`, `keyboard` or `api`. It does not bubble.
events.void-close: Fires before the menu closes, on the menu only (it does not bubble). `detail.reason` is `trigger`, `select`, `escape`, `outside`, `blur`, `parent` or `api`; `preventDefault()` keeps it open when the user caused the close.

events.void-select: Fires when the item is activated by click, Enter or Space; it bubbles to the menu. `detail.value` is the item's `value` and `detail.item` the item element. A disabled item does not fire it.

events.void-open: Fires when the card opens, on hover or focus of the trigger (`detail.reason` is `hover`, `focus` or `api`). It does not bubble.
events.void-close: Fires when the card closes (`detail.reason` is `hover`, `blur`, `escape`, `parent` or `api`). It does not bubble.

void-hover-card.children: Two parts: `void-hover-card-trigger`, wrapping the link or element that opens it on hover or focus, and `void-hover-card-content`, the card.

void-menu.children: Explicit parts, in order: an optional `void-menu-search` around one `<input type="search">` (present means searchable), `void-menu-content` holding the `void-menu-item`s and `void-menu-group`s, and an optional `void-menu-empty` that replaces the default "No results found" while a search matches nothing.

void-menu-group.children: A `void-menu-group-label` heading first, then `void-menu-item` children. The label names the group.

events.void-select: Fires when the item is activated. `detail.value` is its `value` and `detail.item` the item.

void-menu-item.children: The label text, with an optional `void-menu-item-icon` before it and `void-menu-item-shortcut` after it (display only: it does not bind the key).

events.void-open: Fires when the popover opens. `detail.reason` is `trigger` or `api`. It does not bubble.
events.void-close: Fires before the popover closes, on the popover only (it does not bubble). `detail.reason` is `trigger`, `escape`, `outside`, `blur` (focus left it), `parent` or `api`; `preventDefault()` keeps it open when the user caused the close.

void-popover.children: Two parts: `void-popover-trigger`, wrapping the one button that toggles it, and `void-popover-content`, the panel.

void-tooltip.children: Two parts: `void-tooltip-trigger`, wrapping the one element the tooltip describes (it gets `aria-describedby`), and `void-tooltip-content`, the hint text. Put nothing in it the user must read: it appears only on hover or keyboard focus.

events.void-open: Fires when the tooltip appears, on hover or keyboard focus (`detail.reason` is `hover`, `focus` or `api`). It does not bubble.
events.void-close: Fires when the tooltip hides (`detail.reason` is `hover`, `blur`, `escape`, `parent` or `api`). It does not bubble.

void-breadcrumbs.children: One `void-breadcrumbs-list` holding one `void-breadcrumbs-item` per crumb, in order, each holding a link (or text for the current page). The component gives the list and the items `role="list"` and `role="listitem"`. Put `aria-current="page"` on the item of the current page. The separators are drawn by the theme and are not read out.

events.void-open: Fires on the hamburger when the user opens it (`detail.reason` is `trigger` for a click and `keyboard` for Enter or Space). Does not bubble.
events.void-close: Fires on the hamburger when the user closes it (`detail.reason` is `trigger`). Does not bubble.

void-nav-bar.children: A brand, a set of links and controls, laid out in a row: `void-brand`, `void-nav-links`, `void-spacer` and buttons, as in the example.

events.void-open: Fires on the item when it opens its panel. `detail.reason` is `hover` or `trigger`. Does not bubble.
events.void-close: Fires on the item when it closes its panel. `detail.reason` is `hover`, `trigger`, `escape`, `outside` or `blur`. Does not bubble.

void-nav-menu-item.children: Two parts: `void-nav-menu-trigger`, wrapping the one control (a `<button>` that opens a panel, or an `<a href>` that navigates), and for a panel `void-nav-menu-content` with the links. Hover, click, Enter and Space open the panel; a link trigger just navigates.

events.void-change: Fires when the user picks a page. `detail.value` is the page number.

events.void-collapse: Fires when `toggle()` collapses the sidebar. Does not bubble.
events.void-expand: Fires when `toggle()` expands the sidebar. Does not bubble.

void-sidebar.children: The navigation content: links, `void-nav-links` or any markup.

events.void-change: Fires when the user selects a tab. `detail.value` is the `value` of the tab now selected.

void-tabs.children: Explicit parts: a `void-tabs-list` holding one `void-tabs-trigger` per tab (its `value` names the tab, its text is the label, `disabled` disables it), then one `void-tabs-content` per panel with the matching `value`.

void-badge.children: Short text, a count or a status word.

events.void-change: Fires when the visible slide changes. `detail.value` and `detail.index` are the new slide, `detail.previous` the one before.

void-carousel.children: Explicit parts, in order: `void-carousel-content` holding one `void-carousel-item` per slide, then the optional controls `void-carousel-previous`, `void-carousel-next` (empty, with an `aria-label`) and an empty `void-carousel-indicators` that the carousel fills with dots. A control is shown when you write it.

events.void-click: Fires when an `interactive` item is activated.

events.void-sort: Fires when the user activates a sortable header, before the table changes. `detail.column` is the column's key and `detail.direction` the state it goes to (`ascending`, `descending` or `none`). Cancelable: `preventDefault()` keeps the current sort. With `manual`, this is all the table does: the server renders the order.
events.void-filter: Fires once the user has paused typing in the `void-table-filter` part. `detail.filter` is the text, `detail.shown` the rows that match (with `manual`, the rows on the page) and `detail.total` all the rows.
events.void-change: Fires when the user changes the selection with a row checkbox, the select-all checkbox, a Shift range or the select-all-rows offer: once, whatever the number of rows. `detail.value` is the selected row values and `detail.all` is true when the user chose every row across the server's pages.

events.void-remove: Fires when the user presses the remove button of a `removable` tag, just before the tag removes itself from the page.

events.void-copy: Fires after the code was copied to the clipboard, by the control in the `void-code-copy` part or by `copy()`. `detail.value` is the text that was copied: the lines joined by newlines, without line numbers or highlighter markup. It bubbles.

void-code.children: A native `<pre><code>` holding the code (required): the text itself, or one `void-code-line` per line, which `line-numbers` needs. Before it, the optional parts: `void-code-title` (a file name or the language) and `void-code-copy` (wraps the one button that copies the code; leave the button empty for the theme's icon). Inside the `<code>` or a line, any inline markup is kept, so a syntax highlighter's spans go there.

void-diff.children: Explicit parts, in this order: `void-diff-title` (optional; the file name) and one `void-diff-hunk` per hunk. A hunk holds an optional `void-diff-header` (the `@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@` line) and one `void-diff-line` per line, with `kind="add"`, `kind="del"` or no `kind` for an unchanged line, and `old` and `new` for its line numbers. Inside a line, the words that changed go in native `<ins>` and `<del>`; any other inline markup is kept.

events.void-close: Fires when the user presses the control in the `void-alert-close` part, with `detail.reason` `close-button`, just before the alert removes itself from the page. Cancelable: `preventDefault()` keeps the alert. Does not bubble.

void-alert.children: Explicit parts, in this order: `void-alert-title` (optional, short), `void-alert-description` (the message, with any inline markup, such as a link) and `void-alert-close` (optional; wraps the one control that dismisses the alert, and without it the alert cannot be dismissed).

events.void-close: Fires on the banner when the user presses the control in the `void-banner-close` part (`detail.reason` is `close-button`), just before it removes itself from the page. Does not bubble; `preventDefault()` keeps the banner.

void-banner.children: Explicit parts, in this order: `void-banner-title` (optional, short), `void-banner-description` (the message, with any inline markup such as a link), `void-banner-actions` (optional buttons) and `void-banner-close` (optional; wraps the one control that dismisses the banner, and without it the banner cannot be dismissed).

events.void-retry: Fires when the user presses the built-in retry button of a `retryable` fallback. It is the default's: write your own buttons in `void-error-fallback-actions` and listen to them directly.

void-error-fallback.children: Explicit parts: `void-error-fallback-title`, `void-error-fallback-description` (optional) and `void-error-fallback-actions` (optional buttons). Write none and the component writes its built-in default from `heading`, `message`, `retryable` and `retry-label`; write any part and the default goes away, and those attributes no longer apply.

events.void-close: Fires on the toast when it closes, just before it removes itself from the page. `detail.reason` is `close-button` (its `void-toast-close` part; `preventDefault()` keeps the toast), `timeout` or `api` (`close()`). Does not bubble.

void-toast.children: Explicit parts, in this order: `void-toast-title` (optional, short), `void-toast-description` (the message), `void-toast-actions` (optional buttons) and `void-toast-close` (optional; wraps the one control that dismisses the toast). `toast({ title, description, actions })` writes the same parts.

void-toast-container.children: Takes `void-toast` children, written in the markup (a server's flash message) or added by `toast()`. It holds two visually hidden announcers from the moment it connects (a polite `role="status"` and an assertive `role="alert"`); each toast's title and message are written into the matching one shortly after the toast is added (assertive for `error` and `warning`), and the toast itself is a plain `role="group"`, not a live region.

void-accordion.children: Takes `void-accordion-item` children. Without `multiple`, opening one item closes the others.

events.void-open: Fires after the item opens: `detail.reason` is `trigger` (a click), `keyboard` (Enter or Space) or `find` (find-in-page found text inside). Does not bubble.
events.void-close: Fires before the item closes: `trigger` or `keyboard` when the user closed it (cancelable), `outside` when another item opened in a single-open accordion. Does not bubble.

void-accordion-item.children: Two parts: `void-accordion-trigger`, the heading text that opens and closes it, and `void-accordion-content`, the body. The body opens and closes with a height animation (none under reduced motion or `--void-anim-scale: 0`).

void-card.children: Explicit parts, in this order: `void-card-header` (with `void-card-title` and `void-card-description`, and anything that sits at its far end), `void-card-body` and `void-card-footer`.

events.void-open: Fires after the section opens: `detail.reason` is `trigger` (a click), `keyboard` (Enter or Space) or `find` (find-in-page found text inside). Does not bubble.
events.void-close: Fires before the section closes, with `detail.reason` `trigger` or `keyboard`. Cancelable: `preventDefault()` keeps it open. Does not bubble.

void-collapsible.children: Two parts: `void-collapsible-trigger`, the heading text that opens and closes it, and `void-collapsible-content`, the body. The body opens and closes with a height animation (none under reduced motion or `--void-anim-scale: 0`).

void-panel.children: Explicit parts, in this order: `void-panel-header` (optional; with `void-panel-title`, which is also the region's accessible name, and `void-panel-description`) and `void-panel-body`.

void-scroll-area.children: Any content taller or wider than the area; it scrolls inside.

void-bar-chart.children: None. Give the data as the `data` attribute (JSON) or the property; the chart draws a visually hidden data table from it for assistive technology, and `show-table` shows it below the chart.

void-donut-chart.children: None. Give the data as the `data` attribute (JSON) or the property; the chart draws a visually hidden data table from it for assistive technology, and `show-table` shows it below the chart.

void-gauge.children: None. A single reading is the `value`, `min`, `max` and `unit` attributes; segments are the `data` attribute (JSON) or property and colour bands the `zones` attribute or property. A visually hidden data table carries the reading for assistive technology, and `show-table` shows it below the gauge.

void-line-chart.children: None. Give the data as the `data` attribute (JSON) or the property; the chart draws a visually hidden data table from it for assistive technology, and `show-table` shows it below the chart.
